# A2A agents

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/a2a-cards.py from a2a-agents.json. Do not edit by hand:
     change a context's card, then run `scripts/a2a-cards.py --write <gateway>`. -->

Every bounded context exposes one Agent2Agent agent, so another context's agent can
**delegate a goal** to it. Three transports carry three different things and do not
overlap:

| Transport | Carries |
|---|---|
| Kafka + CloudEvents | **facts** between contexts |
| MCP | an agent's **tools** |
| A2A | the **delegation** of a goal; never data sync (delegate out, facts back via CloudEvents) |

The rules are in the fleet rule `agents/fleet/a2a.md`. In short: at most two curated,
goal-shaped skills per agent; a write skill exists only where the context's MCP surface
already offers that write; endpoints are unauthenticated like REST and MCP; problems
are answered in-band as RFC 7807 problems with the REST adapter's status classification.

Cards are served at `/api/a2a/<context>/.well-known/agent-card.json` through the Kong
gateway; the JSON-RPC endpoint is the same prefix (`POST /api/a2a/<context>/`, header
`A2A-Version: 1.0`). A request is a data part
`{"skill": "<id>", "arguments": {...}}`.

**35 agents exposed, 6 write skills.**

## Skills

### inventory-storage

Inventory & Storage agent for the Warehouse Management System: answers how much of a SKU is usable (on-hand minus active reservations and held or unlocated stock, which is what actually constrains a release) and revokes a reservation so its quantity returns to usable.

- **`check_availability`** (read): Read the usable quantity of one SKU: on-hand across all its bins minus active reservations and held or unlocated stock, counted for fleet-owned stock.
- **`revoke_reservation`** (write): Revokes an active reservation, returning its bound quantity to usable inventory so a failed physical delivery never strands an order, and publishes ReservationRevoked (plus the bin stock-level facts) through the transactional outbox.

### product-master

Product Master agent for the Warehouse Management System: tells a delegating agent what a SKU is for handling and physically (description, handling classification, declared and measured unit dimensions and weight, packaging hierarchy), looks a product up from a scanned GTIN, and declares one packaging level with its GTIN under this context's invariants.

- **`product_profile`** (read): Composed read of one product: description and version, its handling classification (tags, temperature class, DOT hazard class; absent when unclassified), its physical profile (declared and latest measured unit dimensions, the effective ones and whether they disagree by more than 10%) and its whole packaging hierarchy, retired levels included.
- **`declare_pack_level`** (write): Declares one packaging level (EACH, INNER, CASE or PALLET) of a registered SKU with its GTIN, exactly as the REST and MCP surfaces do, and publishes ProductPackLevelDeclared (and ProductPackLevelRetired when it supersedes a level) through the transactional outbox.

### facility-layout

Facility Layout agent for the warehouse map: answers what a site physically looks like (zones, aisles, coded storage slots and fixed structures) and how far apart two coded locations are on the map.

- **`site_layout`** (read): Read: one site's full drawable structure as a compact nested map -- zones, then aisles in walk order, then slot codes, with each zone's temperature class and hazmat flag, each aisle's direction and sequence hint, the site's fixed structures, and the site header (name, role in the fulfilment network, transfer capability).
- **`travel_distance`** (read): Read: the shortest travel distance, in metres, between two coded locations (seven-segment codes, e.g.

### slotting-optimization

Slotting Optimization agent for forward pick slotting (read-only): answers where every SKU is slotted right now at a site (the assignments of its Approved slot plan) and reviews a slot plan (its state and policy, the SKU-to-slot assignments with their ABC class, the moves against the previous plan, the SKUs left unassigned and the execution progress of its relocations), either by plan id or as the newest plan of a site and/or state.

- **`forward_slot_map`** (read): Read the CURRENT forward slot map of a site: the assignments (sku, slot, abcClass, pickUnit, casesCapacity for CASE faces) of its Approved slot plan, with that planId and approvedAt.
- **`slot_plan_review`** (read): Read one slot plan in full: siteId, state (Draft, Approved, Rejected or Superseded), policy, the demand window, generatedAt and the decision instants (approvedAt, rejectedAt, supersededAt, each omitted until it happens), rejectReason and supersedesPlanId (omitted when none), the assignments (sku, slot, abcClass, picks, units), the moves against the previous plan (sku, fromSlot, toSlot, kind), the unassigned SKUs with their reason, the version and the execution progress of its relocations.

### inbound-receiving

Inbound Receiving agent for the Warehouse Management System (read-only): answers where an advance ship notice stands in the inbound dock workflow (its state and lines, the receipts counted against it and the Short, Over or Damaged discrepancies they found) and what is booked at the dock doors (carrier appointments by door, state and time window).

- **`asn_receiving_status`** (read): Composed read for one advance ship notice by asnNumber: the ASN (supplierRef, expectedArrival when announced, state Registered, Receiving, Closed or Cancelled, lines with expectedQty) and the receipts counted against it (state Open or Closed, door and appointment when not a walk-in, per-line receivedGood and receivedDamaged, and the discrepancies Short, Over or Damaged: provisional while the receipt is Open, final once Closed).
- **`dock_schedule`** (read): Read the carrier dock appointments in ascending window-start order, optionally only those at one door, in one state (Booked, CheckedIn, Completed or Cancelled) and/or overlapping a from/to range (RFC 3339 instants: from keeps appointments whose window ends after it, to those whose window starts before it).

### pick-face-replenishment

Pick-face replenishment agent for the Warehouse Management System (read-only): answers which forward pick faces of a site are below their minimum, have no reserve source or no policy (with on-hand, reserved and available stock and the policy min/max), and what the replenishment requests that move stock from a reserve bin to a forward bin are doing (Requested, Completed or Cancelled).

- **`pick_face_status`** (read): Read the forward pick faces of one site ordered by forward bin, a page at a time (limit 1..500, default 100): SKU, onHand, reserved and available quantity, the policy minQty and maxQty (absent without a policy), the openRequestId (absent without an open request) and a status: BELOW_MIN (projected level at or below the minimum), OK, NO_SOURCE (below minimum but no reserve bin can supply it) or NO_POLICY.
- **`replenishment_lookup`** (read): Read replenishment requests.

### wes-work-planning

Work Planning & Release agent for the Warehouse Execution System core: reads a process path's live flow status (backlog telemetry plus Drum-Buffer-Rope rebalance recommendation) and admits the next priority-ordered work unit into a path's pool.

- **`flow_status`** (read): Composed read for one process path: backlog telemetry (pending depth, released WIP, feed mode, alarm state) plus the flow-balancing recommendation (NoActionNeeded, ThrottleUpstream, or ReassignLabor).
- **`release_next_work`** (write): Admits the next highest-priority (earliest CPT) pending work unit into a path's work pool, exactly as the REST and MCP surfaces do, and publishes WorkReleased through the transactional outbox.

### fulfillment-execution

Fulfillment Execution agent for the Warehouse Execution System: reports how one process-path queue is doing (pending depth, the most urgent claimable task, claimed tasks whose lease has lapsed or is about to) and completes a claimed task on behalf of the station that holds the claim, under this context's invariants (at-most-once completion, claim ownership, RELOCATE/REPLENISH confirmation).

- **`backlog_status`** (read): Composed read for one process-path queue (PICK, PACK, SLAM, RELOCATE, REPLENISH or BREAK_CASE): the number of Pending tasks, how many tasks a station could claim now with the highest-priority (earliest-CPT) one, and the claimed tasks of that path whose lease has already expired or expires within withinSeconds (default 0 = only already expired).
- **`complete_task`** (write): Completes a claimed task on behalf of the station that holds its active claim, exactly as the REST and MCP surfaces do, and publishes TaskCompleted through the transactional outbox.

### workforce-management

Workforce Management agent for the Warehouse Execution System: answers whether a process path is staffed for a shift (planned vs active heads, with an optional headcount sizing for a charge at a planned rate) and assigns an associate to a path under this context's invariants (one active assignment per associate, certification match, no break, shift not ended).

- **`staffing_status`** (read): Composed read for one process path in one site's committed shift plan: planned vs active heads and whether the path is understaffed.
- **`assign_labor`** (write): Puts an associate on a process path, ending their prior active assignment if any, exactly as the REST and MCP surfaces do, and publishes LaborAssigned or LaborReassigned through the transactional outbox.

### labor-performance

Labor Performance agent for the Warehouse Execution System (read-only): answers how an associate is performing (task count, mean efficiency vs.

- **`associate_scorecard`** (read): Read-only scorecard for one associate: task count, mean efficiency percent (null when no task was scorable), a per-task-type breakdown, a trend (IMPROVING, DECLINING, STABLE or INSUFFICIENT_DATA) and a coaching flag over their most recent tasks.
- **`task_type_status`** (read): Read-only composed status of one task type (PICK, PACK or SLAM) across the whole floor: task count, mean efficiency percent and real measured mean duration (both null when nothing was measurable), the currently-active engineered labor standard (null when none is active, in which case efficiency cannot be scored) and idle-vs-busy utilization over a trailing window (windowSeconds, default 3600).

### task-interleaving

Task Interleaving agent for the Warehouse Execution System (read-only, advisory): tells which interleaving hint a station currently holds and which open tasks it ranks next by travel detour, and gives a site's interleaving overview (its declared policy and how its most recent hints ended).

- **`station_hint_status`** (read): Read where one station stands and what it should take next: its site, its position (location code and the point in metres when the geometry is known), the last task it completed and when, and the hint it currently holds, if any, with its ranked candidate tasks (rank, taskId, taskType, location, detourM).
- **`site_interleaving_overview`** (read): Read how interleaving is set up and behaving at one site: the policy the site declared (maxDetourM, maxCandidates, hintTtlSeconds, eligibleTaskTypes, verticalWeight, version, declaredAt) and its most recent hints, newest first, with how each ended (Active, Consumed, Expired or Superseded) and a count per state.

### process-path-management

Process Path Management agent for the Warehouse Execution System: the read-only source of truth for the fleet's process-path catalogue.

- **`get_process_path`** (read): Read the full definition of one process path by its canonical pathId (e.g.
- **`list_process_paths`** (read): Read the process-path catalogue: every ACTIVE path by default, or, with activeOnly=false, deactivated paths too (the audit view).

### warehouse-planning

Warehouse Planning agent for the Warehouse Execution System: answers whether a registered process path can clear work at a location in a time window (its end-to-end ORDER/HOUR capacity and the bottleneck step) and evaluates the demand assigned to that window against it, recording a DRAFT capacity plan with the shortage.

- **`path_capacity`** (read): Read: the end-to-end capacity of one registered process path at one location for [windowStart, windowEnd) in ORDER per HOUR, the bottleneck step and the constraint binding it, each step's own rate and the composition warnings.
- **`evaluate_capacity_plan`** (write): Write: evaluates the demand assigned to a window against a process path's capacity and records a DRAFT capacity plan (capacity over the window, shortage, bottleneck), exactly as the REST and MCP create-plan operation does, and stores its CapacityPlanCreated CloudEvents in the transactional outbox.

### order-management

Order Management agent for the Warehouse Execution System, the system of record for customer orders.

- **`order_status`** (read): Current state of one order by id: status, allow-partial-shipment flag, promise date and every line's SKU, quantity, process path, gift-wrap, status and reservation id (present only once the line is allocated).
- **`promise_health`** (read): Promise-health KPIs for a time window [from, to) (RFC3339) and an optional exact-match pathId, from the Order Funnel & Allocation Health data product: promise basis distribution (capability-derived CPT window, LeadTimePolicy fallback, or an external network deadline), re-promise rate (fleet-wide, NOT path-scoped: a pathId filter zeroes it), split-shipment rate and the mean promise-to-cutoff gap in seconds.

### network-fulfillment

Network Fulfillment agent for the Warehouse Execution System: the anti-corruption layer between the fleet and the external retail fulfillment network.

- **`network_demand_status`** (read): Read network orders.
- **`advertised_availability`** (read): Read the currently stored CapabilityOffers: the throughput-constrained advertised quantity this context would tell the network it can ship, per SKU and site, and whether that figure is limited by physical stock (PHYSICAL) or by the process path's remaining admission capacity before its next cutoff (THROUGHPUT_CONSTRAINED).

### node-topology

Node Topology agent of the retail network (read-only): answers which delivery station serves a postal prefix, with that station's region and current operational profile (operating hours, cutoffs, handling time, throughput cap), and finds the network's nodes by type, region and status.

- **`serving_station`** (read): Composed read: resolves the delivery station that serves a postal prefix (matched exactly) and returns the assignment (deliveryStationNodeId, regionId, assignmentVersion) together with that station's node: type, operator, region, timezone, location, status and its current operational profile (operating hours, holidays, handling time, cutoffs, throughput cap).
- **`find_nodes`** (read): Lists the network's nodes by id ascending, optionally filtered by type (FULFILLMENT_CENTER, INBOUND_CROSS_DOCK, RETURNS_CENTER, SORTATION_CENTER, DELIVERY_STATION or AIR_HUB), regionId and/or status (PROPOSED, ACTIVE, SUSPENDED or RETIRED); the filters combine with AND and no match is an empty list.

### node-performance

Node Performance agent for the retail network (read-only): answers how a node is performing, from the two scorecards (7-day and 30-day window) this context grades from observed facts only (on-time handover, acknowledgement latency, rejections, expiry, promise-kept rate and inventory feed freshness), and which nodes currently sit at a given grade (A, B, C, D or PROVISIONAL below 50 observations).

- **`node_performance`** (read): Read both scorecards of one node by nodeId: the 7-day and the 30-day window, in that order, each with its state (PROVISIONAL or GRADED), its grade (A, B, C, D, or PROVISIONAL below the observation minimum of 50), its metrics (onTimeHandoverRate, lateAckRate, rejectRate, expiryRate, promiseKeptRate, feedFreshnessP95Minutes, observations) and computedAt, omitted before the first recompute.
- **`nodes_by_grade`** (read): List the scorecards whose current grade matches, ordered by scorecardId ascending, one page at a time: grade is required (A, B, C, D or PROVISIONAL); the window filter (7d or 30d), the page size (limit, 1..500, default 100) and the cursor are optional.

### network-inventory-planning

Network Inventory Planning agent for the Warehouse Execution System, read-only: reports where one inter-warehouse transfer stands (state, quantities, sites, reservation, rejection reason and the full audit trail of state transitions) and finds the transfers that have stopped advancing (non-terminal state unchanged for longer than a threshold, stalest first).

- **`transfer_status`** (read): Reads one inter-warehouse transfer by id: its current state (DRAFT, PROPOSED, APPROVED, ALLOCATING, ALLOCATED, PICKED, IN_TRANSIT, ARRIVED, RECEIVED, UNFULFILLABLE or CANCELLED), sku, quantity, picked quantity, origin and destination sites, reservation id once allocated, rejection reason once unfulfillable, and the audit trail of state transitions (timestamp and cause of each).
- **`find_stuck_transfers`** (read): Finds transfers in a NON-terminal state (RECEIVED, UNFULFILLABLE and CANCELLED are finished and never reported) whose state has been unchanged for MORE than olderThanMinutes, stalest first, with the total number of matches before paging.

### order-sourcing

Order Sourcing agent of the retail network (read-only): answers which vendor node and path will fulfil each shipment group of a customer order, in which state, and why (the promise it must keep, the candidate with its cost, the VirtualQueue release point, the release history, the excluded nodes and the lock and shipment facts).

- **`find_assignments`** (read): Lists the fulfillment assignments (one per shipment group of a customer order), ordered by assignmentId ascending, optionally narrowed by state (QUEUED, RELEASED, LOCKED, SHIPPED, DELIVERED, UNSOURCEABLE or CANCELLED), orderId and nodeId (the candidate node while QUEUED, the node of the latest release later); filters combine with AND.
- **`assignment_detail`** (read): Reads one fulfillment assignment in full by assignmentId: the promise it must keep (tier, deliverByLatest, witness node), its lines, the current candidate node and path with the cost in cost points, the VirtualQueue release point, the whole release history with each outcome (ACCEPTED, REJECTED, EXPIRED, PENDING), the nodes that were excluded and why, and the lock, shipment and delivery facts once they apply.

### delivery-promise

Delivery Promise agent of the retail network (read-only): answers whether the delivery promises of a customer order, or one promise, are intact -- their state, terms, witness path, revisions and the KEPT or BROKEN judgement -- and how full a node's promise books are on a date (share, provisional and confirmed holds per pickup cutoff).

- **`promise_status`** (read): Read the delivery promise(s) behind one customer order: pass orderId for every promise of the order (one per shipment group) or promiseId for one promise.
- **`book_capacity`** (read): Read the promise books of one fulfillment node whose pickup cutoff falls on a date (YYYY-MM-DD, the node's own time zone): per book its state and capacity ledger (share, provisional and confirmed holds), its pickup departure and cutoffAt.

### offer-availability

Offer & Availability agent of the retail network (read-only): answers where an item can be sold and how much is available there (the catalogue item, which nodes list it, whether each listing is LIVE or SUPPRESSED and why, and the quantity a vendor's feed last reported), and what became of one vendor inventory feed (applied, superseded or failed, with its counters and failure code).

- **`check_availability`** (read): Composed read of this context's own listings, narrowed by catalogItemId and/or nodeId (at least one is required).
- **`feed_outcome`** (read): Read one vendor inventory feed by feedId: the node it was sent for (nodeId), whether it was a fullUpdate, its asOf, its state APPLIED, SUPERSEDED or FAILED with the counters (lineCount, appliedCount, staleCount, zeroedCount), receivedAt, appliedAt and, when it FAILED, the failureCode (listing-not-on-node or negative-availability).

### seller-inbound

Seller Inbound agent of the retail network (read-only): the seller-facing front door for stock coming into the network.

- **`seller_compliance`** (read): Answer one seller's rolling-window compliance scorecard from the facts this service recorded: shipments received in the window, cartons reported and received, receiptAccuracyRate (omitted when nothing was reported), discrepancies by kind, discrepancyRatePerShipment (omitted when no shipment closed), compliance violations and the derived complianceTier (GOOD, WATCH or AT_RISK), which is informational only.
- **`inbound_status`** (read): Read the state of one inbound: pass planId for an inbound plan (seller, destination node, packing option, state DRAFT / CONFIRMED / CANCELLED and the declared lines in eaches) or shipmentId for an inbound shipment (plan, seller, destination node, state PLANNED / PACKING / LABELLED / SHIPPED / RECEIVED and every carton packed so far with its SSCC, contents and receipt status).

### vendor-connectivity

Vendor Connectivity agent of the retail network: the read-only Open Host Service for vendors that operate fulfilment nodes.

- **`get_purchase_order`** (read): Read one purchase order released to a vendor, by vendorId and poNumber: state (ISSUED, ACK_PROCESSING, ACCEPTED, REJECTED, EXPIRED, SHIPMENT_PROCESSING, SHIPPED or CANCELLED), nodeId, the windows (issuedAt, requiredShipBy, ackBy), the lines (lineNo, listingId, quantity) and, once they exist, the acknowledgement, the labels, the tracking numbers and shippedAt.
- **`get_node_scorecard`** (read): Read a vendor node's rolling scorecards, by vendorId and nodeId, relayed live from the node-performance context: per window (7d, 30d, 90d) the grade, on-time handover rate, late acknowledgement rate, reject rate, expiry rate, promise-kept rate and feed freshness p95, with the observation count.

### linehaul-transportation

Linehaul Transportation agent of the retail network (read-only): it answers which departures leave a node and how much capacity they still have, and where one departure stands (lane, kind, cutoff/departs/arrives, capacity, booked and remaining packages, state and the cancel/depart/arrive trail).

- **`list_departures`** (read): Read the departure horizon by cutoffAt (then departureId), optionally only departures leaving one origin node (origin), bound for one destination node (destination) and/or whose cutoffAt falls in a window [from, to) (RFC 3339 instants, from inclusive, to exclusive); at most limit rows (1..1000, default 500).
- **`get_departure`** (read): Read one departure by its departureId: lane, kind, origin and destination nodes, cutoffAt (no booking after it), departsAt, arrivesAt, capacityPackages, bookedPackages, remainingPackages and state, plus cancelReason and cancelledAt once cancelled, departedAt once it left and arrivedAt once it arrived.

### last-mile-delivery

Last-Mile Delivery agent of the retail network: the read-only source of truth for a delivery station's waves and for the routes its delivery service partners run.

- **`list_waves`** (read): Read the delivery waves of one station on one service date, ordered by inductCutoffAt: state (OPEN, INDUCTION_CLOSED, DISPATCHED, COMPLETED or CANCELLED), the induct cutoff and delivery window, the stop capacity with assignedStops and remainingStops, and cancelReason on a cancelled wave.
- **`get_route`** (read): Read one route of a delivery service partner: its state (PLANNED, OUT_FOR_DELIVERY or COMPLETED), its numbered stops with the trackingNumbers of each and the outcome derived from the per-package attempts (omitted until every package of the stop has one), and every recorded attempt (trackingNumber, DELIVERED or FAILED, failureReason, at).

### shipping-and-tracking

Shipping & Tracking agent of the retail network: the read-only source of truth for where a package is.

- **`get_journey`** (read): Read the customer-visible journey of one package by its trackingNumber: the state (LABELLED, HANDED_OVER, IN_TRANSIT, AT_STATION, OUT_FOR_DELIVERY, DELIVERED, RETURNED, LOST or VOIDED), the poNumber, assignmentId, orderId and tier of its label, handedOverAt and deliveredAt when they happened, and every stored scan in the order they were recorded, each with its scanType, nodeId, when, and applied (false for a scan stored out of order or without an edge from the state it met).

### returns-processing

Returns Processing agent for the Warehouse Execution System (reverse logistics): the read-only source of truth for return authorizations (RMAs) and the disposition policy.

- **`return_status`** (read): Read the state of returns, addressed by EXACTLY ONE of rmaId (one return authorization) or orderId (every RMA of one original order, ordered by line number then id; an order with no returns, or an unknown one, answers an empty list).
- **`disposition_policy`** (read): Read the disposition policy table: version, returnWindowDays, maxUnitsPerLine, the vetoOutcome a guardrail demotes to, declaredAt and the rules mapping each inspection grade (A, B, C, SCRAP) and product class to an outcome (RESTOCK, REFURBISH, LIQUIDATE, DISPOSE, RTV; "*" is a rule's default product class).

### pricing

Pricing agent for the retail network: answers what a catalogue item sells for right now (state, list price, effective price at this instant, planned and running sale windows) and what a previously issued price quote priced (lines, delivery charges, tax, total, and whether it is still ISSUED or already EXPIRED).

- **`item_price`** (read): Read of one item price by catalogItemId: its state (ACTIVE or WITHDRAWN), list price, the effective price at this instant (the running sale price, else the list price), every sale window with its saleId, price and from/to instants, and the version.
- **`quote_status`** (read): Read of one price quote by quoteId: ISSUED or EXPIRED at this instant (a quote past its expiresAt is EXPIRED whether or not the policy stored it yet), the cart it priced, its lines (unit price and line total), the delivery charge per shipment group, tax, total, the price/schedule/tax-table versions it used, and issuedAt/expiresAt.

### checkout

Checkout agent for the retail storefront (read-only): answers where a checkout session stands, from its state (OPEN, AUTHORIZING, DECLINED, PLACING, REQUOTE_REQUIRED, COMPLETED, EXPIRED or FAILED) to the numbered lines and shipment groups, the binding total and when its quote expires, the payment authorization and the placed order.

- **`checkout_session_status`** (read): Read one checkout session by its sessionId: state, cart and shopper references, numbered lines, shipment groups (groupNo, offerId, tier, lineNos, amountMinor), the binding total and currency, when the price quote expires, the payment authorizationId, the placed orderId, the re-quoted offers of a REQUOTE_REQUIRED session and the failureCode of a FAILED one.

### customer-ordering

Customer Ordering agent of the retail network: the read-only source of truth for placed customer orders.

- **`get_order`** (read): Find out where one customer order stands, by its orderId: its status (PLACED, IN_FULFILLMENT, PARTIALLY_SHIPPED, SHIPPED, PARTIALLY_DELIVERED, DELIVERED, LOST, RETURNED or CANCELLED), the shopper, the destination postal prefix, when it was placed, the cart lines and every shipment group with its promise (promiseId, tier, shipBy, deliverByEarliest, deliverByLatest), its status and revision and any cancellation request or refusal.
- **`get_order_tracking`** (read): Find out how one order is travelling, by its orderId: for every shipment group its promise window, status, lock and ship times, the at-risk and unsourceable signals, the promise verdict (and how many minutes late it ran) and its packages with carrier, state, last scan and exception; a lost or returned group also carries the outcome.

### customer-payments

Customer Payments agent for the storefront: the read-only source of truth for what has been authorized, captured, released and refunded for a checkout session or an order.

- **`get_payment_status`** (read): Read the payment authorizations of one checkout session or one order, or one authorization by id.
- **`get_refund_status`** (read): Read the refunds of one order (oldest first), or one refund by id.

### shopping-cart

Shopping Cart agent for the storefront: a read-only view of a shopper's carts.

- **`get_cart`** (read): Read one cart by its cartId: lines, destinationPostalPrefix, deliveryQuote, selections, the labelled estimate (minor units, estimateComplete says whether every line is priced) and checkoutReadiness.
- **`list_shopper_carts`** (read): Read the carts of one shopper, newest first, optionally of one state (OPEN, CHECKED_OUT, ABANDONED or MERGED).

### product-content

Product Content agent for the storefront domain: answers what a product page needs for one catalogue item (description, bullets, attributes, media and primary category, with its draft/published/retired state and revisions) and what the category tree looks like (every category with its parent and path, at the current tree version).

- **`get_product_content`** (read): Reads the product content of one catalogue item exactly as GET /product-contents/{catalogItemId} returns it: state (DRAFT, PUBLISHED or RETIRED), description, bullets, attributes, media, primary category, revision and published revision.
- **`list_categories`** (read): Reads the whole live category tree exactly as GET /categories returns it: the tree version and every category with its id, parent id, name and path from the root.

### product-discovery

Product Discovery agent for the digital storefront: the read-only source of truth for what a shopper can find and see.

- **`search_products`** (read): Find purchasable products.
- **`get_product`** (read): Read the full view of one catalogue item by catalogItemId: title, hazmat and fragile flags, description, bullets, attributes, media, categoryId and categoryPath (once content is published), list and effective price (once priced), inStock and purchasable.

### exception-management

Exception Management agent for the warehouse (read-only): answers how the open exception caseload sits against its SLA clocks (open, breached, escalated, by severity and queue, optionally with the severity/queue/SLA policy declared per source type) and finds exception cases, one by id or a filtered list by status, queue, site and source type, with their SLA clock, occurrence count, assignee, resolution and audit trail.

- **`sla_status`** (read): How the open caseload sits against its SLA clocks at generatedAt: openCases, breached (open cases past their SLA due time), escalated (cases the SLA sweeper flagged) and the open counts bySeverity and byQueue.
- **`find_exceptions`** (read): Reads exception cases, newest opened first.
